title: The Missing Verdict
premise: When a stranger's corpse is found in the cathedral crypt wearing clothes lifted from Xanthe Ishikawa's own wardrobe, the police reopen a verdict the town buried a decade ago — the disappearance of Judge Amara Voss, whose case files Xanthe has secretly been cataloguing. Following the dead man's paper trail, Xanthe discovers the judge faked her death to escape a corrupt verdict she was coerced into signing, and that the man in his clothes was hired to lure the archivist out as bait. Torn between his growing love for the judge's daughter, the only witness who can identify the killers, and his duty to protect the records that would destroy half the town's founding families, Xanthe stages a public reading of the sealed verdict in the cathedral nave. The trap springs both ways: the killers are exposed, the judge's death is officially reversed, and Xanthe chooses truth over the quiet life of secrets he built, burning the rest of his archive to keep the innocent out of the fire.
about_author: Cyrus Nystrom is the pen name of a former court clerk who spent eleven years transcribing verdicts he wasn't allowed to comment on. He writes mysteries about paper trails, small towns, and the people who keep the records nobody wants read.

chapters.title: The Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Opening the crypt at dawn for a routine inspection, Xanthe finds a dead man wearing his own missing gray coat and shoes, a case number from the closed Voss file pinned to the lapel. The police treat him as a suspect; the town treats him as a curiosity. Emotional beat: the ordered, alphabetized world of the archivist cracks open, and dread replaces the comfort of routine.

chapters.title: What the Judge Left Behind
chapters.summary: Alternating Xanthe and Mara Voss POV. Xanthe deciphers the case number, finding the judge's sealed verdict hidden in a misfiled hymnal, while Mara Voss — the daughter who identified the body as her father's old clerk — arrives demanding answers. Their uneasy alliance forms over shared grief and mutual suspicion. Emotional beat: attraction kindling inside distrust, as both realize the town closed the case too eagerly ten years ago.

chapters.title: The Verdict Everyone Signed
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Following the ledger trail, Xanthe learns the judge's disappearance was staged with the complicity of the town's founding families, and that the dead man was hired to draw the archivist — the last person holding the evidence — into the open. When Mara is nearly run down outside the archive, Xanthe realizes the killers need a witness, and she's it. Emotional beat: loyalty and love collide with duty as Xanthe decides to force the truth public rather than bury it again.

chapters.title: Read Aloud in the Nave
chapters.summary: Alternating Xanthe and Mara POV. Xanthe announces a public reading of the sealed verdict, baiting the killers into the cathedral where the judge herself, alive and hidden for a decade, steps from the crypt to testify. The conspirators are taken; the verdict is reversed; Mara identifies the last name on the ledger. Emotional beat: catharsis and cost — truth wins, the judge's freedom is restored, and Xanthe burns the remaining secret files, choosing a future built on what's said aloud rather than what's filed away.
